title: Run the family Secret Santa with your bot
summary: Your bot handles the busywork of a family or office Secret Santa: it emails everyone their person, passes each wish list to the right gift-giver, and nudges anyone who's late, while you approve every email. A proper draw tool picks the names so nobody, not even you, has to see the matches.
what_the_bot_does: Takes everyone's names, email addresses, the gift limit and the rules (no spouses, no repeat from last year).
Runs the draw with a Secret Santa tool (website or connector), so the matches are truly random and stay hidden, then sends each person their own private link or email.
Drafts a friendly kick-off email in your voice with the budget, the date and how to send a wish list.
When a wish list arrives, drafts the email passing it on to that person's Secret Santa (without saying who's who to anyone else), and waits for your OK.
On a date you pick, reminds anyone who hasn't sent a wish list yet.
what_you_end_up_with: A Secret Santa that runs itself: everyone knows their person, wish lists reach the right gift-giver, and you didn't have to keep the secret or chase anyone.

tools.note: Can give itself an email address and draft each email for you to approve; one mom of eight ran an 18-person Secret Santa this way
Can connect a Secret Santa MCP server (secretsanta.name) that runs the draw and emails private links without showing the matches to the assistant
Same Secret Santa connector works in Claude

prompt:
Help me run our Secret Santa for [number] people. Gift limit: [amount]. Exchange date: [date].

People and emails: [name - email, name - email, ...]
Rules: [these couples can't draw each other: ...] and nobody gets the same person as last year: [last year's pairs, or 'no list'].

1. Don't pick the names yourself. Use a Secret Santa draw tool (or tell me which free one to use) so the draw is random and the matches stay hidden, including from me.
2. Draft a short kick-off email in my voice: the budget, the date, and 'reply with your wish list by [date]'. Show me before sending.
3. When a wish list comes in, draft an email passing it to that person's Secret Santa only. Show me each one before it goes out.
4. On [reminder date], draft a friendly nudge to anyone who hasn't sent a list.

Never send anything without my OK, and never tell anyone (including me) who has whom.
setup: Pick an assistant that can send email for you after you approve: Grok Bot (it can make its own email address), ChatGPT or Claude with a Secret Santa connector, or ChatGPT dots.

For the draw itself, use a Secret Santa tool: a free website (DrawNames, Elfster) or a Secret Santa connector such as secretsanta.name's MCP server, which runs the draw and emails each person a private link without telling the assistant the matches.
Tell the family the emails will come from your bot's address, so they add it to their contacts and check spam.
Paste the prompt, check the kick-off email, then approve each send.
A few days in, ask the bot: 'Has everyone received their person? Which emails are still waiting for my OK?'
watch_out: Approval queues are easy to miss. The mom who ran an 18-person Secret Santa with Grok Bot found 12 emails waiting but she'd only approved 9, so 3 kids never got their person (X @sjpusey, Nov 10; Agents 101). Ask the bot to list what's still waiting.
Don't let a chatbot 'randomly' pick names. In one test ChatGPT and Gemini said 7 every time when asked for a number from 1 to 10 (38 asks) (X @oddorithm, Nov 20). Use a draw tool or names in a hat.
If you're playing too, a plain chat can't hide the draw from you. Use a draw tool that emails people directly, or let someone who isn't playing run it (X @NewAIShortcut, Nov 18).
Older relatives may struggle with sites that make them log in to see their person (Reddit r/ChristmasGiftIdeas). Pick a tool that just emails the name.

sources.label: X post by @sjpusey (2026-11-10): 'I just used my Grok bot to do Secret Santa for my household.' Eight kids plus four spouses; no spouses drawing each other, no repeats from last year (4 likes / 3 replies / 114 views, measured 2026-11-23)

Agents 101 write-up of the same story: the bot made its own email address, drafted each email in her voice, forwarded each wish list to the right Santa and reminded late ones; she approved every send, and 3 of 12 emails sat unapproved until she checked
secretsanta.name: Secret Santa MCP server for ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor (create_draw, send_invites, wish lists; 'No tool returns the assignment', so the assistant never learns who has whom)

Reddit r/ChristmasGiftIdeas, 'A good secret Santa website' by u/mydude333 (2026-10-07): parents struggle with sites that need a login and code; commenters suggest DrawNames, Elfster, 'Alternately ChatGPT will do the same thing' (4 points / 22 comments as shown)

X post by @oddorithm (2026-11-20): asked for a number from 1 to 10, ChatGPT and Gemini said 7 every time (38 asks); use a Secret Santa generator or names in a hat (1 like / 1 repost / 38 views, measured 2026-11-23)
